title: LLM Value Functions for Credit Assignment in Agentic RL
abstract: arXiv:2610.15840v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for large language model (LLM) agents remains challenging in long-horizon tasks with sparse outcome rewards, where assigning credit to individual actions is difficult. Methods such as GRPO assign the same trajectory-level advantage to all actions, while critic-based methods require learning an additional value function that can be costly and unstable. We introduce LLM Value Function RL (LVRL), which uses the pretrained knowledge and in-context learning ability of an LLM to estimate policy-aware state values without finetuning a separate critic. LVRL conditions the value model on group context and calibrates its predictions using known values at the initial and terminal states, enabling step-level credit assignment from estimated value differences. translated_title: 用于智能体强化学习中信用分配的LLM价值函数
translated_abstract: 将强化学习（RL）应用于大型语言模型（LLM）智能体时，在具有稀疏结果奖励的长时程任务中仍然充满挑战，因为在这种情况下很难为单个动作分配信用。诸如GRPO之类的方法为所有动作分配相同的轨迹级优势，而基于评论家（critic）的方法则需要学习一个额外的价值函数，这可能代价高昂且不稳定。我们提出了LLM价值函数强化学习，该方法利用LLM的预训练知识和上下文学习能力来估计策略感知的状态价值，而无需微调单独的评论家。LVRL以组上下文为条件构建价值模型，并使用初始状态和终止状态的已知值来校准其预测，从而能够通过估计的价值差异实现步级信用分配。我们进一步将这一思想扩展到通过在线策略蒸馏（OPD）从专家策略中学习，提出了LLM价值函数在线策略蒸馏（LVOPD），其专注于教师……
tldr: 该论文提出LVRL方法，利用LLM的预训练知识与上下文学习能力来估计状态价值，无需训练额外的评论家即可实现长时程稀疏奖励任务中的步级信用分配，并进一步扩展出LVOPD以实现从专家策略的在线蒸馏学习。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes LVRL, which leverages LLMs' pretrained knowledge and in-context learning to estimate state values, enabling step-level credit assignment in long-horizon sparse-reward tasks without training a separate critic, and further extends it to LVOPD for on-policy distillation from expert policies.
